target_customer: Hospital clinical teams: physicians, residents, interns and medical students
problem: Clinicians kept patient lists on paper or shared them by SMS and camera phones, which is insecure. ListRunner gave a HIPAA-compliant digital patient list shared within a care team.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to hospitals and clinical teams (pricing not found)
product_category: Healthcare team collaboration and patient sign-out app

founders.name: Jeeshan Chowdhury
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (July 2014) spells the name Chowdury. He was finishing medical school when he noticed the problem.

founders.name: Dominic Savoie
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch calls him an engineer; the YC page calls him co-founder and CTO.

founders.name: Trevor Chan
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch calls him Dr. Trevor Chan.

competitors.name: Paper patient lists
competitors.what: Printed lists and handwritten sign-out, plus informal SMS and photos
competitors.traction_then: the standard practice per the founder

competitors.name: Electronic medical records
competitors.what: EMRs, not designed for ward-level team collaboration per the article

technical_complexity.rationale: Cross-platform iOS and Android app with HIPAA-compliant sharing of patient data, which adds security and compliance work for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Hospital adoption brings some lock-in, but EMR vendors and messaging apps could add similar sign-out features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Health tech roll-up Commure acquired it; the date and terms are not confirmed in a primary source.

market_need_then: In July 2014 the founder told TechCrunch the biggest competitor was paper, and a private beta ran in 15 hospitals worldwide after a Hacking Health debut in Cape Town.

branding.domain_note: Used listrunnerapp.com (suffix variant); it now redirects to commure.com.

rebrands.why: Product kept its name under Commure per the App Store listing; date not stated.

brand_strength.rationale: Modest healthcare press coverage; the name survived as a Commure product but no community or brand evidence found.

outcome_analysis: ListRunner was founded by doctors who built a secure patient list app after seeing paper and SMS sign-out, entered YC in summer 2014 and ran a beta in 15 hospitals. It was later sold to Commure, which still lists a Listrunner app, but the deal date, price and the company's funding are not confirmed in primary sources, so the strength of the outcome is unknown.
notes: Funding seen only in aggregators and a MobiHealthNews headline about a 500,000 dollar raise (page returned 403): Dealroom says about 620,000 dollars in two 2014 rounds, CB Insights 520,000 dollars, so all unverified and not recorded as rounds. The October 2017 acquisition date is from CB Insights only and unverified. A hedged Dealroom claim that Dock Health continues ListRunner was ignored. Chowdhury's later bio on selling ListRunner to Commure came from a search summary of an Aspen Ideas bio, not opened. Founded year not stated in a source.
